children: Livestock futures fall with hogs setting new contract lows and cattle snapping a five-session winning streak. The USDA's cold storage report showed beef in freezers at the end of October up 5% from the previous month and 2% above their year-earlier level. Frozen pork supplies were down 5% from the end of September but up 8% on the year. "The reports for both beef and pork are not good news," Chris Lehner of ADM Investor Services says in a note. "Beef imports into the U.S. along with high priced beef are putting U.S. beef in storage," he says. The pork industry, meanwhile, "needs to have a deep discounted sale in order to reduce the problem of pork storage." Live cattle fall 1.2% on CME to $2.26975 a pound. Lean hogs fall 1.8% to 55.425 cents a pound. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
